licensed_photos.caption: The May 23, 2019 view shows red bench rows, stair aisles with handrails, chairback rows and the multi-level pavilion. It was photographed during the period when FC Cincinnati used Nippert. Full frame retained; resized and converted to WebP.

licensed_photos.author: Greenstrat

licensed_photos.title: Loch Norse bridge and railings — 2008
licensed_photos.alt: A plank bridge with black railings crosses Loch Norse toward a paved lakeside path, with NKU’s Fine Arts Center behind it.
licensed_photos.caption: The source dates this full-frame view May 31, 2008. It shows the bridge decking, side railings, shadows from overhead beams and part of the lakeside path beside the Fine Arts Center. Converted to WebP without cropping or retouching.

licensed_photos.limitations: Historical outdoor-route context only. This does not identify the current designated accessible entrance or establish a continuous route from parking to the building. Deck condition, gaps, width, slope, thresholds and present-day operation are unverified; do not infer that the bridge is required for arrival.

linked_guides.title: Arena stairs, concourses and seating-edge railings
linked_guides.description: The supplier’s one-page case study contains seven photographs: a seating-bowl overview, upper seating stairs, suite-seat edges, concourse railings, the grand staircase, the Suite 08 approach and a platform edge the supplier labels an ADA section. These are views of the renovation completed in November 2018; the PDF has November 2023 metadata, and individual capture dates are unknown. It does not show a complete entrance-to-seat route, elevator operation, toilets or current ticket allocation. The supplier’s compliance wording is not an independent access audit. Photographs remain with their publisher; no reuse licence was found.
linked_guides.documentDate: November 2023 PDF metadata; renovation completed November 2018

linked_guides.title: Arena entrance plaza, wayfinding and concourse photographs
linked_guides.description: The architect’s project page contains nine photographs and a separate design sketch. The entry-hall photo shows an overhead sign pointing toward the ticket office, Champions Club and elevator; other views show the plaza, door rows, concourse and Armory Bar, seating bowl, and a team corridor. The final comparison includes the old pre-renovation frontage, a sketch and the completed frontage; the sketch is not a photograph. Individual capture dates are unknown, and the project completion year is 2018. A sign does not establish the elevator’s location, operation or a continuous route. Team and premium areas are not necessarily open to every visitor. No reuse licence was found; images remain with the architect.

linked_guides.title: Storefront steps and partial ramp
linked_guides.description: Brighton Center’s program page includes one storefront photograph showing the Thrifting on Eastern sign, number 2014 on the porch post, front steps and a railed ramp running along the facade toward the porch. The lower ramp approach is beyond the right edge. The doorway is in shadow; threshold, door controls, slope, width and a complete sidewalk-to-shop route cannot be verified. Capture date and current route operation are unknown. No reuse licence was found, so the photo remains on Brighton Center’s page.

linked_guides.title: Redden Gardens fridge, shelves and kiosk approach
linked_guides.description: Three relevant Redden Gardens photographs on the operator’s broader page show the fridge shelter and rough paved foreground, open pantry shelves with a microwave and water dispenser to the side, and the wellness kiosk beside the fridge. The kiosk sits on a raised concrete pad; a cardboard pile is visible beside it in that view. Photos do not establish a step-free approach, door force, shelf/control reach, available stock or current obstructions. Capture dates are unknown; the filename “fridge-2026” is not a verified photo date. The separately labeled Banklick photo shows another location. No reuse licence was found; these images remain on COVUnity’s site.

linked_guides.title: Concert hall, theatre seating and outdoor amphitheater views
linked_guides.description: Seven photographs on NKU’s facilities page include Greaves Concert Hall from the audience, Corbett Theatre from the stage, an outdoor amphitheater with concrete tiers and handrails, the building by the lake, and gallery, rehearsal and practice-room scenes. The Corbett view shows stepped seating aisles with small edge lights; it does not locate accessible seating. Several images contain performers or visitors, and teaching rooms are not public quiet spaces. Capture dates are unknown and images may predate later Fine Arts renovations. Current layouts, alternate routes, toilets and door controls are unverified. No reuse licence was found; the photographs remain on NKU’s page.

linked_guides.title: Fine Arts frontage, paving and benches
linked_guides.description: One university photograph shows the facade labeled Gallery / NKU Corbett Theatre, paved foreground, benches beside grass, and distant dark entrance doors. The sign identifies the building but does not identify the glass-door arrival point in SOTA’s current directions. Capture date, paving gradients, thresholds, door controls and a continuous route from parking are unverified. No reuse licence was found; the image stays on NKU’s building-information page.

linked_guides.title: Museum gallery passages, displays and lighting
linked_guides.description: Nine photographs on the 2019 renovation designer’s project page show carpeted passages between exhibit cases, a red floor line, display islands, wall screens, the broadcasting desk, baseball-card area and the Champions Gallery’s large video wall. Lighting varies across the photographed rooms, but still images cannot establish brightness levels, sound or flashing effects. Some views contain visitors. Individual capture dates are unknown; the photographs do not establish current layouts, door widths, counter reach, restrooms or the elevator route. No reuse licence was found, so the images remain with the designer.
linked_guides.documentDate: 2019 renovation project; individual photo dates unknown

linked_guides.title: Exhibit passages, seating and wraparound screens
linked_guides.description: The museum’s Exhibits page has 70 inspected photographs and a separate Big Red Machine graphic. Useful views include a short row of red seats facing an exhibit screen, red upholstered benches and angled touchscreens in the Hall of Fame Gallery, carpeted passages between display cases, pull-out baseball-card panels and the Champions Gallery video wall. Many other images are close-ups of artifacts, not access routes. Several photos also appear on the 2019 designer page; a currently available webpage does not establish when a photo was taken. Capture dates, present layout, screen motion/flashing, sound levels, seat dimensions, toilets and elevator access remain unverified. Images stay on the Reds’ page; no reuse licence was found.
linked_guides.publisher: Cincinnati Reds Hall of Fame and Museum
linked_guides.documentDate: Current exhibit webpage; individual capture dates unknown

WE BELIEVE
It takes a community of support.
WE BELIEVE in partnering with individuals and families to help them 
reach financial stability and independence. During our last fiscal 
year, we impacted the lives of 27,194 individuals, from infants to older 
adults, across all eight counties of Northern Kentucky and beyond. 
Knowing that the challenges families and communities face are 
often complex and that making positive changes require long-term 
holistic and comprehensive services, Brighton Center provides a true 
community of support through our 47 programs.

HIGHLIGHTS
Through a donation from St. Elizabeth 
Healthcare, Thrifting on Eastern opened as 
a social enterprise located at 2014 Eastern 
Ave in Covington, KY. The thrift store offers 
affordable clothing, accessories, decor, and 
household items. All proceeds from the thrift 
store go directly back into supporting our 
Family Support programs.
We continued our commitment to advancing 
diversity, equity, and inclusion. This allowed 
staff to come together and have explicit 
conversations about race, along with 
increasing their education and awareness 
on racial equity. We also finalized our Racial 
Equity Strategies and started implementing 
them across the organization.
FY 21 marked the first full year implementing 
our new agency wide database, which 
launched at the end of 2019. This powerful 
tool will help us serve individuals and families 
more efficiently and effectively. It will also 
advance our ability to impact entire families by 
showing what combination of programs move 
a family to economic stability. 
Brighton Center was recognized as a winner 
of the 2020 Cincinnati Torch Award for 
Marketplace Ethics for extraordinary business 
operations and ethics. The Better Business 
Bureau (BBB) Torch Award for Marketplace 
Ethics is a significant honor for the entire 
Brighton Center team. This award affirms 
the community’s trust in us, which is built on 
accountability and transparency.
Youth Services received approval by the 
Department for Community Based Services 
as a Qualified Residential Treatment 
Program operated at Homeward Bound 
Shelter. This allows youth to receive long-
term placement and intensive services.

For a family struggling to make ends meet, asking for help is often a last resort after exhausting all 
of their resources. Staff work in partnership with customers to solve the individual and unique set 
of challenges that bring each customer through our doors to ensure their basic needs are met and 
goals for the future are within reach. We provide long-term support and guidance for families as they 
overcome barriers. Our home visitation programs ensure even our youngest customers have the tools 
and resources necessary to build a solid foundation for the future. 
FAMILY SUPPORT
Family Support is a crisis intervention program intended to help individuals 
and families with emergency needs. Families receive referrals and linkages 
to services that enable them to stabilize through case management and 
supportive wrap around services.
STABLE FAMILIES
Stable Families serves families with children in grades K-3 who are at 
imminent risk of homelessness to stabilize their housing situation. The goal is 
for parents to maintain housing while children maintain school stability.
RAPID REHOUSING AND STREET OUTREACH
Rapid ReHousing and Street Outreach works with individuals experiencing 
homelessness to connect them with quality, affordable housing, and wrap 
around support services. 
NEIGHBORHOOD COMMUNITY GARDEN
The Community Garden has 96 raised beds, allowing residents to increase 
knowledge of ways to grow food and cook nutritious meals.
SAFETY NET ALLIANCE
Safety Net Alliance was established to increase the efficiency and 
effectiveness of safety net services provided to Northern Kentucky 
residents in need. This collaborative of over 150 partners includes large and 
small nonprofits, faith-based organizations, public agencies, educational 
institutions, and funders. 
THRIFTING ON EASTERN
Thrifting on Eastern is a community thrift store that offers high-quality, gently 
used household items and clothing at affordable prices. 
EVERY CHILD SUCCEEDS (ECS)
Every Child Succeeds provides in-home parenting education, and support for 
new moms, dads, and babies in Campbell, Boone, Grant, and Kenton Counties. 
Home Visitors meet with families weekly and focus on healthy pregnancy 
outcomes, optimizing child development, and growing strong families. 
Through hands-on activities, curriculum discussion, family/child groups, 
and a strength-based approach, families can increase the emotional bond 
between parent and child, build parental confidence, and enhance family 
self-sufficiency. 
HOME INSTRUCTION FOR PARENTS OF PRESCHOOL 
YOUNGSTERS (HIPPY) 
HIPPY provides Home Visitation services for Boone, Campbell, and Kenton 
County families with children ages 2-5 that focus on helping parents prepare 
their preschool age children for success in school. Home Visitors help parents 
mingle learning and play as a part of the curriculum.

Cindy and Jeri, volunteers in our 
Food Pantry and members of the 
Americorps Seniors Volunteer 
Program work alongside staff to 
provide food and personal care items 
to customers by unloading donations, 
stocking pantry shelves, and assisting 
customers picking up food for their 
families, all while providing a friendly 
and welcoming environment.
Ken, a volunteer who drives Brighton 
Center’s truck, picks up food 
donations from local retail stores. 
He helps to unload the truck and 
works alongside our Food Pantry 
volunteers to ensure individuals 
accessing services have fresh food 
and nonperishables. Additional 
volunteers will also deliver food to 
home-bound adults later in the day.
Brighton Recovery Center for Women 
residents volunteer their time by 
giving back at Thrifting on Eastern 
where they assist with sorting 
donations, stocking shelves, helping 
donors who are dropping off items, 
and ensuring an all around wonderful 
shopping experience for customers. 
Staff from a local business volunteer 
at Saratoga Place Apartments, one of 
our three senior living communities. 
Half of the volunteer group hosts 
an enthusiastic game of bingo 
while another group helps Brighton 
Properties with landscaping and 
beautification of the outdoor spaces 
for residents to enjoy. 
Erica, Brighton Recovery Center 
Alumni and Food Services Manager 
for CENTER TABLE, Catering with a 
Purpose, and her mom, Linda, host 
a Family Night to provide support 
to family members of women at the 
Recovery Center. Volunteering is an 
important part of our self-sufficiency 
continuum.  
 
 
Members of Brighton Center’s Junior 
Board, a young professionals group 
dedicated to volunteerism, advocacy, 
and fundraising, spend some time 
with youth at Homeward Bound 
Shelter. Together, they help the youth 
celebrate special holidays throughout 
the year. This often opens the door 
to informal mentoring opportunities 
for youth. 
Learn more:
volunteer@brightoncenter.com 
brightoncenter.com/volunteer
Board Members participate in Board 
Days of Service, an annual volunteer 
initiative for our Board of Directors. 
They connect with individuals at 
Center for Employment Training and 
conduct virtual mock interviews 
with individuals to prepare them for 
upcoming job interviews.
The PLUG, an outlet for creative energy 
which combines artistic passion 
with community service, leads a 
community art project at City Heights 
with residents and Youth Leadership 
Development club members. The PLUG 
has also led art projects with several 
Brighton Center programs ranging
from youth to older adults. 
1,174 caring volunteers provided 12,457 
hours of service to support Brighton Center 
programs during our last fiscal year.
